risk: The 16-step number is attributed to the wrong mechanism; operators reasoning about minimisation depth (RFC 9156 §2.3) get the wrong bound.
suggestion: Change both to 'max 10 minimisation steps (RFC 9156 §2.3)' or reference DefaultMaxRecursionDepth separately for the walk.

title: Spoofguard row: 'reject AR=0+NOERROR+EDNS' inverts the actual rejection signature
description: ARCHITECTURE.md:124 documents spoofguard as rejecting 'AR=0+NOERROR+EDNS', which reads as rejecting an EDNS-bearing NOERROR response. The code (server/upstream/plain/udp.go:443-447) rejects non-EDNS responses lacking a CNAME and with AN<2 — i.e. the ABSENCE of EDNS is the GFW signature. FLOWCHARTS.md:282 states it correctly ('GFW signature: AR=0 + NOERROR without EDNS').
risk: The two docs contradict each other; a reader may think EDNS-bearing responses are dropped, the opposite of the behavior.
suggestion: Reword to 'reject AR=0 + NOERROR WITHOUT EDNS (bare A/AAAA, GFW signature)'.

title: Exported Detector type lacks a doc comment
description: internal/ipdetect/ipdetect.go:13 declares `type Detector struct` with no doc comment (only its fields TraceURL etc. are commented). The package comment (line 1) describes the package, not the type. Note this is a distinct exported Detector from server/defense's Detector, so the ambiguity is real.
risk: godoc shows an undocumented exported type; two exported Detector types in the repo make the missing doc more confusing.
suggestion: Add a type doc, e.g. '// Detector discovers the machine's public IP via external HTTP endpoints (default ifconfig.me) with fallback order.'

title: 10 exported PQ crypto functions lack doc comments
description: internal/dnscryptcrypto/pq.go exports HKDFSHA256 (46), PQCertContext (62), PQDeriveSharedKey (85), PQResumeSecret (101), PQResumedSharedKey (114), PQEncapsulate (131), PQDecapsulate (135), PQOpenTicket (175), PQParseControlBlock (213), EncodeTicketPlaintext (262) — none carry a doc comment, unlike the surrounding code which documents layout constants and control-block semantics. This package is a fork of dnscrypt-proxy crypto but lives under internal/ and is audited as project code.
risk: The security-sensitive PQ KEM/ticket API is undocumented; e.g. PQResumeSecret/PQResumedSharedKey nonce-truncation and ticket-scope rules are only discoverable by reading implementations.
suggestion: Add one-line godoc to each function (the certificate.go layout constants already document offsets — reference them).

title: EDNS VERSION never inspected — no BADVERS response per RFC 6891 §6.1.3 MUST
description: RFC 6891 §6.1.3 (archived, line 466-469): 'If a responder does not implement the VERSION level of the request, then it MUST respond with RCODE=BADVERS.' ZJDNS never reads the request OPT's VERSION field: middleware/edns.go:32-39 forces a full unpack and inspects only Pseudo options (ECS/Cookie/Padding); no code anywhere reads the OPT TTL bits 16-23 (grep for Ttl>>16 / Version() / RcodeBadVers across server/ and edns/ finds nothing — the only RcodeBad* matches are RcodeBadCookie=23, a different code). The response OPT is synthesized by ApplyToMessage (edns/edns.go:94-107), which sets msg.UDPSize and msg.Security only; miekg/dns v0.6.87 (dns.go:196) states 'Version is the EDNS version, always zero'. A client sending an EDNS query with VERSION=1 therefore receives a normal version-0 response instead of the mandated BADVERS(16).
risk: Protocol non-compliance on an RFC MUST; EDNS-version probing tools (e.g. edns-version checks) and future EDNS versions will misidentify the server as supporting VERSION>0, and the server will silently process queries under an unsupported version contract.
suggestion: In the EDNS middleware after full unpack, read the request OPT version (opt.Hdr.TTL >> 16 & 0xFF via the OPT.Version() accessor in miekg/dns v0.6.87) and, if nonzero, reply RCODE=BADVERS with an OPT carrying the server's version (0) instead of delegating into the chain.

title: Six RFCs cited in production code are not mirrored in docs/rfc/ (violates project guideline #1)
description: CLAUDE.md guideline 1 and docs/rfc/GUIDELINE.md state the project mirrors all referenced RFCs locally (50 files archived). Six RFCs cited by production code are absent: RFC 7958 (8 cites: trust_anchor.go:71,118,124; dnssec_chain.go:81,305,425), RFC 6895 (2: middleware/validation.go:71,98), RFC 4343 (2: dnssec/extract.go:40, dnssec/nsec.go:30), RFC 3597 (2: resolver/zonecut.go:99, dnssec/nsec.go:436), RFC 9147 (1: server/upstream/tls/dtls.go:38), RFC 3225 (1: edns/edns.go:102). Section claims inside these cites (RFC 7958 §3.2 XML KeyTag/digest, RFC 6895 §3.1 opcode/class rules) are therefore unverifiable against the local archive.
risk: Reviewers and future maintainers cannot validate the DNSSEC trust-anchor, case-insensitivity, unknown-RR-type, DTLS 1.3, and DO-bit claims against the authoritative text the project promises to keep locally; RFC 7958 §3.2 governs trust-anchor integrity and RFC 3597 governs unknown-type wire handling in the zone cut — both security-relevant.
suggestion: Mirror rfc7958.txt, rfc6895.txt, rfc4343.txt, rfc3597.txt, rfc9147.txt, rfc3225.txt into docs/rfc/ (and update GUIDELINE.md if it enumerates the archive), or re-anchor the comments to RFCs already archived.

title: Malformed cookie lengths 9-15 and >40 get BADCOOKIE instead of the RFC 7873 §5.2.2 FORMERR
description: RFC 7873 §5.2.2 (archived, lines ~390-400): cookie total lengths 9-15 ('shorter than the minimum COOKIE option with both a Client Cookie and a Server Cookie (16 bytes)') and >40 ('longer than the maximum valid COOKIE option (40 bytes)') MUST produce FORMERR; valid lengths are exactly 8 and 16-40. The code path: ParseCookie (edns/cookie.go:277-301) accepts any length >= 8 and strips the first 8 bytes as client cookie; middleware/edns.go:84-89 then returns BADCOOKIE whenever the remaining server-cookie length is nonzero and != 16 — so totals 9-15 (server portion 1-7) and >40 (server portion >32) produce BADCOOKIE(23), never FORMERR. Also, the FORMERR comment cites 'RFC 7873 §5.3' (middleware/edns.go:72 and cookie.go:275), but §5.3 is 'Processing Responses' (client-side); the malformed-length rule is §5.2.2.
risk: Slightly wrong error code to clients with pathological cookies; RFC 7873 §5.2.2's FORMERR semantics (reject the request) are replaced with a BADCOOKIE that the client may retry pointlessly, and the wrong §5.3 citation misleads maintainers.
suggestion: Classify by total cookie length: <8 or 9-15 or >40 -> FORMERR; 17-40 (invalid server cookie) -> BADCOOKIE per §5.2.4/§5.2.2; fix the two §5.3 comments to §5.2.2.

title: RFC 4034 section citations wrong in crypto.go: §2.1.2 for SEP bit and §3.1.1 for RRSIG signer name
description: crypto.go:145 says 'The SEP bit is a deployment convention (RFC 4034 §2.1.2)' — RFC 4034 §2.1.2 is 'The Protocol Field' (value 3); the SEP bit (Flags bit 15) is specified in §2.1.1 'The Flags Field' (archived rfc4034.txt:212-243). crypto.go:100 says 'RFC 4034 §3.1.1: the RRSIG signer name must be the DNSKEY's owner name' — §3.1.1 is 'The Type Covered Field'; the signer-name rule is §3.1.7 'The Signer's Name Field' (rfc4034.txt:481). Both comments cite real RFC 4034 text but point at the wrong subsections.
risk: Misleading citations in the DNSSEC validation core; a maintainer chasing a signer-name/SEP bug via the cited sections will read the wrong field definitions.
suggestion: Change crypto.go:145 to 'RFC 4034 §2.1.1' and crypto.go:100 to 'RFC 4034 §3.1.7'.

title: RFC 8767 nonexistent subsections cited: §5.2 (line 54) and §4.2 (line 68)
description: RFC 8767 sections 4 ('Standards Action') and 5 ('Example Method') are flat — no §4.2 or §5.2 subsections exist (verified against archived rfc8767.txt: sections at lines 149 and 185, no sub-numbering). defaults.go:54 'DefaultServeExpiredClientTimeout = 600ms // RFC 8767 §5.2: short wait before serving stale' — the client-response-timer concept is §5 (recommended 1.8s). defaults.go:68 '// RFC 8767 §4.2: timeout SHOULD default to less than 10 seconds' — the query-resolution-timer guidance ('commonly around 10 to 30 seconds') is also §5, not §4.2.
risk: Cited sections do not exist in the archived RFC; the 'SHOULD default to less than 10 seconds' attribution to §4.2 is fabricated section-wise and slightly overstates the RFC text (which describes a range, not a MUST/SHOULD value).
suggestion: Rewrite both comments to cite 'RFC 8767 §5' (Example Method: client response timer / query resolution timer).

title: Three wrong section citations: RFC 8484 §4.1.2, RFC 6604 §1.1, RFC 768 §3.1
description: (a) https_dns.go:109 'RFC 8484 §4.1.2: DoH serves only standard DNS QUERY semantics' — RFC 8484 §4.1 has only subsection §4.1.1 'HTTP Request Examples' (grep '4.1.2' in rfc8484.txt: no match); the DoH request requirements live in §4.1 itself. (b) nameserver.go:93 'RFC 6604 §1.1: NXDOMAIN may include CNAME/DNAME records' — RFC 6604 §1.1 is 'Conventions Used in This Document'; the xNAME/NXDOMAIN RCODE rule is §3 'RCODE Clarification' (rfc6604.txt:157). (c) probes.go:128 'valid per RFC 768 §3.1' — RFC 768 (User Datagram Protocol) has no numbered sections at all (verified: the archived rfc768.txt contains no section numbering).
risk: Nonexistent section pointers in transport-layer comments degrade the RFC cross-reference discipline the repo otherwise maintains (~90% of ~130 citations verified correct).
suggestion: Point to RFC 8484 §4.1, RFC 6604 §3 (or §4 Security Considerations), and drop the RFC 768 section number (cite 'RFC 768' alone).

title: Comment claims 'all other accept loops sleep on retry' — DTLS accept loop is the exception and can spin at 100% CPU
description: The comment at lines 77-78 ('Temporary error: back off too, or a sustained condition spins at 100% CPU (all other accept loops sleep on retry)') claims every other accept loop backs off. Verified against all native accept loops: tls.go:70, quic.go:102, http3.go:88, tlcp.go:79, dtlcp.go:268-281 (50ms) all sleep on accept error — but server/protocol/tls/dtls.go:90-96 continues with no sleep in EITHER branch (temporary and non-temporary errors both just `continue`). The claim is contradicted by the code, and the DTLS listener is exposed to exactly the 100% CPU hot-spin the comment warns about (e.g. sustained EMFILE or garbage-UDP Accept errors).
risk: Misleading comment hides a real defect: under sustained accept errors the DTLS accept loop spins at 100% CPU with no backoff, unlike every other listener in the server.
suggestion: Add `time.Sleep(config.DefaultAcceptRetryDelay)` in the dtls.go accept loop's error branches (matching quic.go:102 / tls.go:70), or if intentional, fix the comment to name DTLS as the exception.

title: concurrencyLimit comment: 'drop ... 10 to 8 at 20→21 servers' is arithmetically wrong (actual raw drop is 10→7)
description: Comment (lines 254-258) says the raw tier formulas 'drop from 8 to 7 at 12→13 servers and 10 to 8 at 20→21'. Verified against the constants (tier1=4, tier2=12, tier3=20, div2=2, div3=3, lines 120-124): first claim is correct (tier2 at 12 = (12*2+2)/3 = 8; tier3 raw at 13 = (13+1)/2 = 7). Second claim is wrong: raw at 20 = (20+1)/2 = 10, raw at 21 = 21/3 = 7 — the drop is 10→7, not 10→8. The monotonicity floors (max(...,8) for tier3, max(DefaultMinConcurrencyLimit=8, 10) for default) still make the returned values monotonic, so behavior is unaffected.
risk: Misleading comment: a maintainer reasoning from the documented numbers (10→8) about the fan-out floor will misjudge the tier formulas.
suggestion: Correct the comment to '10 to 7 at 20→21 servers'.

title: Four sequential errors.As calls in isQUICRetryable replaceable with errors.AsType[T] (Go 1.26)
description: isQUICRetryable (lines 226-247) does four errors.As(err, &T) checks for *quic.ApplicationError, *quic.IdleTimeoutError, *quic.StatelessResetError, *quic.TransportError. Go 1.26 (go.mod go 1.26.4) provides errors.AsType[E error](err) (E, bool), already used in this codebase at internal/dnsutil/dnsutil.go:225 (IsTemporaryError). The identical var+As pattern also appears at server/protocol/tls/dtls.go:144, server/protocol/tlcp/dtlcp.go:325, cmd/zjdns/cli/probe.go:313, server/upstream/tls/https.go:114, and server/handler/middleware/cache_store.go:191 — 10 sites total remain on the old form.
risk: None functional; inconsistent with the codebase's own errors.AsType usage and more verbose than the standard idiom.
suggestion: Rewrite each site as e.g. `if qAppErr, ok := errors.AsType[*quic.ApplicationError](err); ok { ... }`.

title: sort.Slice in PrefetchCooldown.Cleanup — should be slices.SortFunc per project standard
description: Line 78: `sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].ts < entries[j].ts })` sorts the cooldown map snapshot before evicting the oldest half. This is the only sort.Slice/sort.SliceStable in production code. Go 1.26 slices.SortFunc is the idiomatic replacement and CLAUDE.md explicitly states the project standard ('slices.SortStableFunc over sort.SliceStable'). Since this sort runs on the prefetch path whenever the cooldown map exceeds DefaultPrefetchCooldownMaxEntries, it is also the intended per-package home for this pattern.
risk: None functional; style drift from the project's stated Go-version idiom.
suggestion: Replace with `slices.SortFunc(entries, func(a, b entry) int { return cmp.Compare(a.ts, b.ts) })` (imports slices and cmp).

title: Hand-written reverse scan loop in UnPad replaceable with slices.Backward
description: UnPad (lines 132-146) implements the ISO/IEC 7816-4 padding removal with a manual `for i := len(packet); ; { ... i-- ... }` loop. This is the only production reverse-iteration loop in the repo (grep of `for i := len(...)`, `; i >= 0; i--` found only this, the excluded siphash test, and server/resolver/resolver.go:248 which is a genuine Fisher-Yates shuffle and must not be changed). Go 1.23+ `for i := range slices.Backward(packet)` expresses the same scan; the 0x80-delimiter and MinDNSPacketSize checks transfer directly (packet[0]==0x80 is rejected via i < MinDNSPacketSize in both forms).
risk: None functional; verbose, easy-to-misread loop in a per-query crypto path.
suggestion: Rewrite with `for i := range slices.Backward(packet) { ... }` and return ErrInvalidPadding after the loop.
